comment_styles: BINARY QUESTION: ask a question comparing two things from the video, answerable with a single letter (A/B). Pattern: 'Which is crazier: A or B? Just type the letter.'
PERSONAL RECALL: ask something the viewer can answer in one word from their own experience ('How old were you when you learned this?').
VALIDATION: write a line that invites agreement OR objection — both produce comments ('Tell me I'm not the only one who got chills').
FIND THE GAP: 'I left out one detail on purpose — can you find it?' Send the viewer back into the video. (NEVER state false information — authority is the product.)
connective_styles: BREAK THE EXPECTATION: imply the explanation now forming in the viewer's head is WRONG. Don't reveal the right one yet.
SCALE UP: hint that the number or fact you just gave is small compared to what's coming.
HIDDEN ACTOR: announce there is a cause BEHIND this that you haven't named yet.
COUNTDOWN: say a threshold is approaching — then cut, without saying 'and then'.
OPEN A CONTRADICTION: signal that a fact contradicts what you just said.
IMPLY A COST: say this ability has a price. Withhold the price.
MAKE IT PERSONAL: imply this is happening in the viewer's own body or life.
TURN AT THE LAST MOMENT: start with 'but' and invert the picture you just painted.

series.header: This is EPISODE {no} of '{title}'. The next one will be number {next_no}.
series.paying_promise:
THIS EPISODE PAYS A PROMISE. The previous episode promised the viewer:
  "{promise}"
The PEAK of the video (peak_beat) must pay exactly THIS promise. The viewer subscribed for this answer; tell them anything else and the trade is broken — they won't trust you again.
series.announce_arc: ANNOUNCE THE SERIES: this is the FIRST episode of a {arc_total}-EPISODE series called '{arc_title}'. Somewhere in the narration (not in the hook — after the peak), say in one sentence that the series runs {arc_total} episodes and where it is going. Nobody subscribes to a video; people subscribe to a SERIES.
series.finale:
THIS IS THE LAST EPISODE OF '{arc_title}'. The arc closes here:
  • Leave the 'open_loop' field EMPTY — the next episode arrives with a NEW topic.
  • But the series is NOT over: after the peak, say in one sentence that episode {next_no} lands tomorrow and opens a NEW subject.
series.planned_loop:
OPEN DOOR — ALREADY WRITTEN, DO NOT INVENT. The topic of the next episode ({next_no}) is:
  "{next_topic}"
  • Put THIS TOPIC verbatim into the 'open_loop' field.
  • Name the SAME subject IN THE BEAT AFTER THE PEAK too, in your own words, and hand it to episode {next_no}. NOT in the closing — the subscribe chip appears on screen exactly then; if the promise hasn't been spoken yet, the ask lands on nothing.
    ✗ 'But the story doesn't end here.'   ← says nothing about what is coming
    ✓ 'But that light isn't the fish's own — the bacterium that makes it is episode {next_no}.'
series.chain_loop:
OPEN DOOR — MANDATORY. This episode pays its own peak IN FULL, but does not close: it leaves a new and SPECIFIC subject that the peak itself exposed, and its answer is in episode {next_no}. This requires TWO SEPARATE OUTPUTS:

  1) The 'open_loop' FIELD = THE NEXT EPISODE'S TOPIC (never spoken).
     This text will be used VERBATIM as episode {next_no}'s production topic.
     No episode number, no 'next time', no 'I'll explain' — the topic ONLY.
     ✗ 'I'll reveal this secret in episode {next_no}.'
     ✓ 'The symbiotic bacterium that produces the anglerfish's light'

  2) THE BEAT AFTER THE PEAK = the SPOKEN cliffhanger.
     Name the same subject THERE, in your own words, and hand it to episode {next_no}. NOT in the closing — the subscribe chip appears exactly then; an unspoken promise makes the ask land on nothing.
     ✗ 'But the story doesn't end here.'   ← says nothing about what is coming
     ✓ 'But that light isn't the fish's own — the bacterium that makes it is episode {next_no}.'

  BOTH must share the same subject (overlapping words): the field NAMES it, the beat SPEAKS it.
series.teaser_fallback: This is an episode of the '{title}' series. End the closing with an OPEN LOOP / teaser that makes the viewer curious about the next episode ('the next one is even stranger').
